labels.label: def:manifold_future_complete_all

hypotheses.paper: for all x ∈ M~, D(J⁺(x)) = J⁺(D x) and D(I⁺(x)) = I⁺(D x)
hypotheses.note: GX.IsFutureComplete C D is the literal definition for any causality C. For a BTZ-manifold M, GX.BTZTildeData.IsBTZFutureComplete applies it to the chart-generated causality of (M~, T') (BTZTildeData.causality). DEC-77 (b), its former authority, is reversed by DEC-106; its J± are those of the natural causality natCausality (natCausality_le_top_iff), its I± are not. Read literally with natCausality the definition is unsatisfiable as soon as sing M ≠ ∅: at a BTZ point x, D(I⁺(x)) = D(∅) = ∅ ≠ I⁺(D x) (GX.BTZTildeData.not_isFutureComplete_natCausality). Model non-vacuity of the T' reading: GX.btzJ0_isFutureComplete. Independence of y0 and Φ not proved.

findings: DEC-27 under DEC-106: with the natural causality of M~ (≪ between regular points only), def:manifold_future_complete_all (l.2343) is never satisfied once sing M ≠ ∅ (GX.BTZTildeData.not_isFutureComplete_natCausality); the definition is formalized for the chart-generated ≪ of (M~, T_BTZ), a reading pending a ruling. Previous REPORT's 'Content unchanged' is withdrawn: the content is unchanged but its DEC basis moved.
questions: Under DEC-106, is 'future distinguishing' (l.2317, used at l.2325 and l.2359) and 'future complete' (l.2343) for M~ to be read (A) for the chart-generated chronological relation ≪ of (M~, T_BTZ) — GX.BTZTildeData.causality, whose ≤/J± coincide with the natural causality's, the reading under which isFutureDistinguishing_of_base and IsBTZFutureComplete are proved; or (B) literally for the natural causality GX.BTZTildeData.natCausality (≪ only between regular points, since the natural topology forbids an open I⁻(y) containing a BTZ point — argued), under which l.2325 (BTZ~ half), l.2343 and l.2359 are FALSE (counterexamples proved) and the strongest true form is 'I⁺(x) = I⁺(y) iff x = y or both are BTZ points' (natIplus_eq_iff); or (C) by another notion (e.g. distinguishing by J⁺, or I⁺ restricted to reg)? Accepting (A) or (B)-with-the-corrected-form would let the master re-mark lem:globally_hyperbolic_manifolds_maximal, the BTZ~ half of lem:globally_hyperbolic_manifolds_manifolds, and def:manifold_future_complete_all.

labels.label: lem:globally_hyperbolic_manifolds_manifolds

hypotheses.note: charted form (ChartedSpace E0Y, e0Groupoid, chartedCausality, [T2Space M], DEC-66 (a)) and SingularGXStructure form (e0ManifoldCausality); this half is fully proved

DEC-106: M~ with its natural topology and GX.BTZTildeData.natCausality; GH = causal + naturally compact diamonds. Literal conclusion FALSE once sing M has two points (BTZ points all have I⁺ = ∅: not_isFutureDistinguishing_natCausality). Proved: (i) strongest true natural form, natural GH ⇒ (I⁺(x) = I⁺(y) iff x = y or both BTZ) (natIplus_eq_iff_of_natGloballyHyperbolic); (ii) mixed reading, natural GH ⇒ FD for the chart-generated ≪ of (M~, T') (isFutureDistinguishing_of_natGloballyHyperbolic). Natural GH is NOT shown satisfiable for any instance with sing M ≠ ∅.

findings: DEC-27 under DEC-106: in the natural topology no causality can carry the geometric ≪ at BTZ points (argued, not formalized: a natural neighbourhood of a BTZ point s is a whole component of p⁻¹(U), on which D is unbounded, so I⁻(y) ∋ s is not naturally open). With natCausality (≪ between regular points) every BTZ point has I⁺ = ∅ (natCausality_Iplus_eq_empty), so the BTZ~ half of l.2325 is false as soon as sing M has two points (not_isFutureDistinguishing_natCausality, via surjectivity of M~ → M); the strongest true form is injectivity on the regular part plus separation of regular from BTZ points (natIplus_eq_iff_of_natGloballyHyperbolic).

The previous REPORT's non-vacuity argument ('the natural topology is coarser, so a T_BTZ/Minkowski-compact diamond is naturally compact') is WITHDRAWN: diamonds with a BTZ vertex are exactly the T_BTZ-noncompact ones, and no Minkowski-pulled-back topology on M~ is shown finer than the natural one. Natural GH of an instance with sing M ≠ ∅ is not established. What is proved instead is the model non-vacuity of the coarser-topology route: the diamonds of J⁺(Δ₀) are compact in Minkowski space (GX.btzJ0_isCompact_val_image_diamond; J⁺(Δ₀) is a future set), so the T_BTZ model is future distinguishing (GX.btzJ0_isFutureDistinguishing) although not T_BTZ-GH.

The tarentin-free argument (GX.le_of_Iplus_eq_of_isCompact_image_diamond): from I⁺(x) = I⁺(y), x ∈ Z⁺ and q ≫ x, x is a limit of points of I⁺(y) ∩ I⁻(q) ⊆ J(y,q), which is compact hence closed, so y ≤ x; it replaces ETT's GH ⇒ strongly causal route, unavailable because natural diamonds have empty interior at BTZ points (argued).

sorries.decl: (not stated — strict file; the dispatched route 'M GH ⇒ lift of a Cauchy surface is Cauchy ⇒ M~ GH (natural topology)')
sorries.obstruction: Not delivered. Natural GH of M~ needs, for J(x,y) ⊆ M~ with p(J(x,y)) ⊆ J_M(px,py) compact: (i) a finite-sheet lemma — over each evenly covered U ⊆ reg M only finitely many sheets of p⁻¹(U) meet J(x,y) (the fibres of M~ → M are infinite, so lean-causal's only covering GH proof, Causal.Flat.Cla.isCompact_diamond_of_isFiniteCover, which uses finite fibres for compactness of p⁻¹(J(px,py)) and a finite sheet-label set, does not apply); (ii) a limit step at BTZ sheets — natural convergence to a BTZ end does not give D-convergence (D is not naturally continuous there), so closedness of J needs D-boundedness on the diamond, Minkowski-convergence through the parabolic quotient of the lifted chart, and 'D u ≤ D w inside a causally convex lifted chart ⇒ u ≤ w'. lean-causal also has no Cauchy-surface ⇒ GH (Geroch converse) nor limit-curve theorem for the Cauchy-surface route. Each is a multi-hundred-line development on MaxBranchedCover/Fox ends; not attempted beyond the analysis. The paper's l.2359 conclusion does not need it (both readings proved from M GH directly).

findings: DEC-27 under DEC-106: with the natural causality of M~, l.2359 is FALSE as soon as sing M has two points: every BTZ point of M~ has empty natural chronological future (natCausality_Iplus_eq_empty), M~ → M is onto (exists_not_mem_regPart), so two BTZ points have the same I⁺ (GX.BTZTildeData.not_isFutureDistinguishing_natCausality). Strongest true form, proved from M GH with no added hypothesis: I⁺(x) = I⁺(y) iff x = y or x, y are both BTZ points (GX.BTZTildeData.natIplus_eq_iff).

l.2361 'not different from the proof for Lorentzian manifolds' (M GH ⇒ M~ GH ⇒ FD): with T_BTZ (DEC-77 (b), reversed by DEC-106) the middle step is false in the model (GX.btzJ0_not_isCompact_diamond, GX.btzJ0_not_globallyHyperbolic, GX.btzJ0Tilde_not_globallyHyperbolic) — kept as a recorded finding; in the natural topology it is not proved (obstruction above), and even granted, natural GH yields only the strongest true form (natIplus_eq_iff_of_natGloballyHyperbolic), not literal FD.

The proof that is used: the projection M~ → M is causal (proj_le), equal (natural or T') chronological futures force D x = D y and p x = p y (closures of I⁺, J⁺ closed in Minkowski space and in the GH M), and a causal chain from y to a point z ≫ x near x stays over a causally convex V (strong causality of M) inside a sheet on which (p, D) is injective (eq_of_dev_eq_of_proj_eq, shared by both readings). For the natural form the point z is taken regular, which the T'-openness of the regular part allows (exists_natIplus_mem_of_reg).

kb_proposals: GH ⇒ future distinguishing without tarentin: Z⁺ in a finer topology where I⁻(q) is open plus compact diamonds in a coarser Hausdorff one suffice (GX.isFutureDistinguishing_of_isCompact_image_diamond). Use it whenever the topology carrying compactness is not the one where ≪ is open.

A natural open of M~ is T'-open by preimage under the continuous identity d.toNat (GX.BTZTildeData.natOpens); a T'-open subset of p⁻¹(reg M) is naturally open by nhds_reg (isOpen_inter_regPart). A T'-causal curve is a natural causal curve because CurveOn quantifies over opens N.

Covering-space GH in lean-causal exists only for FINITE covers (Causal.Flat.Cla.isCompact_diamond_of_isFiniteCover); M~ → M has infinite fibres — do not expect to reuse it without the finite-sheet and BTZ-sheet limit lemmas.

In the natural (Fox) topology of M~ no Causal.Causality carries the geometric ≪ at a BTZ point (argued): natCausality keeps ≪ between regular points, so I⁺ = ∅ at every BTZ point and literal 'future distinguishing' / 'future complete' FAIL (GX.BTZTildeData.not_isFutureDistinguishing_natCausality, not_isFutureComplete_natCausality). The strongest true FD form is 'I⁺ x = I⁺ y ↔ x = y ∨ both BTZ' (natIplus_eq_iff). Do not certify an FD row on natCausality without a ruling.
A causality whose Z⁺ is only a subset still yields pointwise FD from compact diamonds: GX.le_of_Iplus_eq_of_isCompact_image_diamond needs Z⁺ at x alone.
